subject: Scaling & unit-econ comparison — next tests and pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan@startupx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next tests: scaling, per-1M token economics, and pilot

Ethan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: move from POC -> pilot for the customer-facing assistant (multi-turn generation mixed with embeddings for retrieval).
- Traffic profile: peak bursts of ~120 RPS, typical seq lengths 64-256, 30–40% short completions.
- Key evaluation axes for StartupX: latency p95, per-1M token unit cost, and cache behavior for repeated prompts.

High-level unit-econ comparison (ballpark numbers to align expectations)
- Redwood Hosted (default): ~$16–18 per 1M tokens (with batching + prefix cache assumptions, 60% avg cache hit).
- OrionCloud hyperscaler (self-hosted endpoints): ~$22–28 per 1M tokens (claims high throughput, but higher baseline instance costs; cold-cache tests show >2x token cost).
- AtlasAPI (third-party inference API): ~$20–24 per 1M tokens, but limited batching and no KV prefix caching.

Why Redwood looks different for this workload
- Prefix/KV caching reduces token generation by ~30–60% for repetitive assistant turns; we keep model behavior consistent (no re-sampling) while shaving cost.
- Continuous batching and dynamic kernel selection maintain p95 latency while improving token/sec on GPUs.
- Routing to lower-cost model variants with function-call fallback preserves UX in overload cases.

Proposed benchmark matrix (what we should run next)
1) Cold vs warm cache (scripted sample set) — measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost/1M; target cache-hit probes: 0%, 30%, 60%, 90%.
2) Batch sizing sweep — batch sizes 1 / 4 / 16, seq lengths 64 / 256; measure throughput and tail latency.
3) Quantized model variant — 4-bit quantized run vs fp16 baseline for token-cost delta and quality spot-checks.
4) Hyperscaler parity run — run equivalent workload on OrionCloud endpoints (StartupX to run or provide creds) so we compare apples-to-apples.

Attachments: I attached a quick econ snapshot with the raw assumptions (startupx-econ-snapshot.xlsx) and a short bench run instruction doc (redwood-benchmark-instructions.md).

Next steps / asks
- Ethan: please confirm procurement contact (cc'd when available) and whether StartupX can provision a short OrionCloud test endpoint or provide traffic replay.
- Ben / Marissa: if we can greenlight a 3-test bench (cold/warm/cache + batch sweep + quantized run) we can commit to a pilot pricing outline.
- I'll coordinate scheduling — target start: next Tue (2028-12-10) if that works for StartupX.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 04 Dec 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Recap + next tests — engineering ask (bench run scope)

Forwarding Ethan's note — Rishi, can you own the bench runs? Key asks below (short):
- Run the matrix Jordan proposed against the 'assistant' prompt set attached (startupx-sample-queries.json).
- Bench variants: baseline fp16, 4-bit quantized, and fallback smaller model.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens (based on instance time + utilization), and measured cache-hit %.
- Cache scenarios: cold (no warm KV), partial warm (seeded with 30% of keys), warm (seeded to 60%/90% as separate runs).
- Batch sweep: 1 / 4 / 16. Sequence lengths: 64 / 256.
- Deliverable: consolidated CSV + short slide with charts (target EOD Fri 12/08).

Ben — if Rishi confirms resource/time, please draft a pilot price recommendation for StartupX so procurement has something to look at. We should be prepared to offer a 90-day pilot with committed usage.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan / team — I can own the runs. Quick plan and clarifications below:

Plan
- I will create three bench jobs on the internal cluster: (A) baseline fp16, (B) 4-bit quantized build, (C) fallback small-variant (faster but lower quality). Each job will run the same query replay three times for consistency.
- For cache scenarios: I'll seed KV cache with the provided sample set to reach ~30% and ~60% hit rates; warm/cold will be scripted. We'll also run a synthetic 90% warm run to show upper bound.
- Batch sweep and seq lengths per Jordan's matrix.
- Quality spot checks: sample 100 completions from each variant and flag any degenerations (RAG checks will be manual).

Implementation notes
- Using the continuous-batching runtime on the bench cluster to match production serving.
- I'll instrument p50/p95 latency with existing tracing and compute cost/1M tokens by combining GPU utilization time with our internal cost model (will include assumptions in the CSV).

Deliverables and timeline
- Raw CSVs + bench-config.yaml (attached)
- Summary slide with token-cost delta and recommended config for pilot by EOD Fri 2028-12-08.

If anyone has additional probes to include (e.g., token-quality regression tests or special tokenization cases), flag now.

Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
